text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to $126.04, continuing a seven-day slide that has now wiped out 7.8% from its price. The decline reflects mixed signals in the oil market: while geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have kept global oil prices elevated at $114.89 a barrel, U.S. crude has slumped to $96.41—a sign that markets are pricing in the possibility of a ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran. Since ConocoPhillips is a major producer whose profits rise with oil prices, a narrowing of the risk premium built into global crude weighs on its stock.

Adding to the pressure, a potential diesel export ban under consideration by the Trump administration threatens refining margins—the profit oil companies make when they process crude into fuel. News commentary earlier this week noted that export restrictions could disrupt the market in ways that actually hurt U.S. refiners and ultimately consumers, which has likely dampened investor sentiment around energy stocks broadly.
